natural: red-lacquered gates and embroidered doors

meaning.en: The grand residence of a rich and powerful family.
meaning.zh: 指富贵人家华丽的住宅。

examples.zh: 朱门绣户的背后，往往藏着不为人知的辛酸。
examples.en: Behind the grand mansions there is often hidden hardship.

examples.zh: 小说里写了朱门绣户与茅檐草舍的鲜明对比。
examples.en: The novel sets grand mansions sharply against thatched huts.

examples.zh: 他从小生在朱门绣户，却向往平淡的生活。
examples.en: Born in a wealthy household, he nevertheless longed for a simple life.

usage.en: Mostly attributive or object; literary, used for contrast with poor homes.
usage.zh: 多作定语或宾语，书面语，常与贫寒人家对比。

natural: hating the house, hating even its crows

meaning.en: To dislike someone so much that one dislikes everything connected with them.
meaning.zh: 因为憎恨某人，连与他有关的一切人和事物也都憎恶。

examples.zh: 他讨厌那个老板，恨屋及乌，连他的公司产品都不买。
examples.en: He dislikes that boss so much that he won't even buy his company's products.

examples.zh: 她和前任分手后恨屋及乌，再也不去那家餐厅。
examples.en: After the break-up she hated everything linked to her ex and never went back to that restaurant.

examples.zh: 不能因为恨屋及乌就否定他全部的贡献。
examples.en: You cannot dismiss all his contributions just because you resent everything about him.

usage.en: Predicate. The negative counterpart of 爱屋及乌.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，是“爱屋及乌”的反面说法。

natural: a clan living together

meaning.en: To live together with all one's clan or kin in the same place.
meaning.zh: 同一家族的人聚集在一起居住。

equivalents: live as a clan in one place

examples.zh: 这个古村落的居民聚族而居，几乎都姓陈。
examples.en: The villagers of this old settlement live as one clan, almost all surnamed Chen.

examples.zh: 客家人多聚族而居，围屋就是例证。
examples.en: The Hakka often lived clustered by clan, as their walled houses show.

examples.zh: 南方不少地区至今保留着聚族而居的传统。
examples.en: Many parts of southern China still keep the tradition of clan settlement.

usage.en: Predicate; descriptive of settlement patterns in history, sociology or travel writing.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于描述历史、社会或旅游中的居住形态。

natural: pipes, song and dance at a banquet

meaning.en: Music, singing and dancing at a lavish banquet; a scene of merrymaking.
meaning.zh: 笙乐歌唱、宴饮舞蹈，形容盛大热闹的游乐场面。

equivalents: a night of song and dance

examples.zh: 王府里夜夜笙歌燕舞，百姓却饥寒交迫。
examples.en: The prince's mansion held song and dance every night while the people starved.

examples.zh: 春节晚会上笙歌燕舞，热闹非凡。
examples.en: The New Year gala was full of music and dance, lively beyond words.

examples.zh: 诗人笔下的江南，处处笙歌燕舞。
examples.en: In the poet's Jiangnan, music and dancing could be heard everywhere.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; literary, sometimes hinting at idle luxury.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，书面语，有时带有奢靡之意。

natural: prosperous people, abundant wealth

meaning.en: A prosperous population and plentiful wealth.
meaning.zh: 人民富裕，财物丰盛。

examples.zh: 史书称贞观年间国泰民安，民殷财阜。
examples.en: Histories describe the Zhenguan years as peaceful and prosperous.

examples.zh: 这座古城曾经民殷财阜，商贾云集。
examples.en: This old city was once wealthy and thronged with merchants.

examples.zh: 他治理一方，终使当地民殷财阜。
examples.en: His rule at last made the region prosperous.

usage.en: Predicate; formal or historical writing, about a place or an era.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，用于书面语或史述，形容地方或时代。

natural: twisted arguments and wicked doctrines

meaning.en: Fallacious arguments and misleading doctrines.
meaning.zh: 不合正理、荒谬有害的言论和学说。

examples.zh: 别听他那一套歪理邪说，事实根本不是这样。
examples.en: Don't listen to his specious arguments; the facts are nothing like that.

examples.zh: 网上流传着许多歪理邪说，我们要学会分辨。
examples.en: Plenty of bogus theories circulate online, and we must learn to tell them apart.

examples.zh: 老师批评他用歪理邪说为自己的懒惰辩护。
examples.en: The teacher criticised him for defending his laziness with specious arguments.

usage.en: Object or subject; always disapproving.
usage.zh: 多作宾语、主语，含贬义。

natural: go to the wilds and become a bandit

meaning.en: To become an outlaw or bandit, usually by being driven to it.
meaning.zh: 指进入山林做强盗，多是被逼无奈。

examples.zh: 林冲被逼得走投无路，只好落草为寇。
examples.en: Driven into a corner, Lin Chong had no choice but to become an outlaw.

examples.zh: 灾荒之年，不少农民落草为寇。
examples.en: In famine years many peasants took to banditry.

examples.zh: 他宁可饿死，也不愿落草为寇。
examples.en: He would rather starve than turn bandit.

usage.en: Predicate; typical of historical fiction such as 《水浒传》.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常见于《水浒传》等历史小说。

natural: defeated but not disheartened

meaning.en: Not to lose heart after a defeat.
meaning.zh: 遭到失败后并不气馁。

equivalents: pick oneself up after a loss

examples.zh: 球队虽然输了比赛，却败而不馁，继续刻苦训练。
examples.en: The team lost, but undaunted, kept training hard.

examples.zh: 创业失败后，他败而不馁，很快又开了新公司。
examples.en: After his start-up failed he was not discouraged and soon founded another company.

examples.zh: 我们要学会胜而不骄，败而不馁。
examples.en: We must learn to stay modest in victory and undaunted in defeat.

usage.en: Predicate; often paired with 胜而不骄.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与“胜而不骄”连用。

natural: immune to every poison

meaning.en: Immune to all poisons; also used humorously of someone who is never affected by germs, insults or harm.
meaning.zh: 任何毒物都伤害不了；也常戏指不怕脏、不怕病或不怕批评。

examples.zh: 武侠小说里的主角常练就百毒不侵之身。
examples.en: The heroes of martial-arts novels often acquire bodies immune to all poisons.

examples.zh: 他吃什么都没事，大家都说他百毒不侵。
examples.en: Nothing he eats ever upsets him; everyone says he is immune to everything.

examples.zh: 被网友骂了这么多年，她早已百毒不侵。
examples.en: After years of online abuse she has become impervious to it.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; literal in fiction, jocular in daily speech.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语；小说中指实义，口语中多为戏称。

natural: the moon wanes and the flowers fade

meaning.en: A scene of decline and loss; also a couple's parting or lost happiness.
meaning.zh: 月亮残缺，花朵凋残；比喻美好事物的衰败，也指夫妻离散、幸福不再。

examples.zh: 词中月缺花残的意象，写尽了她的哀愁。
examples.en: The imagery of waning moon and faded flowers in the poem conveys all her sorrow.

examples.zh: 经历了月缺花残的变故，他对爱情不再抱幻想。
examples.en: After the heartbreak of lost happiness he no longer held illusions about love.

examples.zh: 昔日的庭院如今月缺花残，一片荒凉。
examples.en: The old courtyard, its beauty gone, now lies desolate.

usage.en: Literary; used in poetry and sentimental writing.
usage.zh: 书面语，多用于诗词和抒情文字。

literal: feel · present · cherish memory of · past
natural: moved by the present, thinking of the past

meaning.en: To compare the present with the past and be filled with emotion.
meaning.zh: 面对今天的情景，回想过去，感慨万千。

equivalents: muse on how things have changed

examples.zh: 重返母校，他不禁感今怀昔。
examples.en: Returning to his old school, he could not help comparing then with now.

examples.zh: 老人站在旧居前，感今怀昔，泪湿衣襟。
examples.en: The old man stood before his former home, recalling the past, his sleeves wet with tears.

examples.zh: 这篇散文感今怀昔，情真意切。
examples.en: This essay looks back on the past with genuine feeling.

usage.en: Predicate; literary and wistful.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，书面语，带怀旧感伤的色彩。

natural: what was entrusted was to the wrong person

meaning.en: To have placed one's trust or affairs in the wrong hands.
meaning.zh: 把事情或终身托付给了不可靠的人。

equivalents: entrust something to the wrong person

examples.zh: 公司交给他打理，结果亏损严重，真是所托非人。
examples.en: The company was left in his care and lost heavily; the trust was misplaced.

examples.zh: 她后悔所托非人，嫁了个不负责任的丈夫。
examples.en: She regretted trusting the wrong man, having married an irresponsible husband.

examples.zh: 事已至此，只怪自己所托非人。
examples.en: It has come to this; I can only blame myself for trusting the wrong person.

usage.en: Predicate; often in hindsight or regret.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于事后追悔。

pinyin: shì wèi zhī jǐ zhě sǐ
literal: scholar · for · know · self · one · die
natural: a gentleman will die for one who truly understands him

meaning.en: A person of principle will give his life for someone who truly appreciates him.
meaning.zh: 有气节的人愿为真正赏识、了解自己的人献出生命。

equivalents: die for a friend who understands you
loyalty to one who values you

examples.zh: 士为知己者死，他决心报答老板的知遇之恩。
examples.en: A man will die for one who truly values him, and he resolved to repay his boss's trust.

examples.zh: 古人讲士为知己者死，重的是那份信任。
examples.en: The ancients said a gentleman dies for his true friend, valuing that trust above all.

examples.zh: 他对这位恩师始终怀着士为知己者死的感激。
examples.en: He felt a deep, devoted gratitude toward this mentor.

story.en: The assassin Yu Rang, avenging his lord Zhibo, said: 'A gentleman will die for one who knows him, as a woman adorns herself for one who delights in her' (士为知己者死，女为悦己者容).
story.zh: 豫让为智伯报仇，说：“士为知己者死，女为说（悦）己者容。”

usage.en: Often quoted with the second half, 女为悦己者容. Said of loyalty and gratitude for being appreciated.
usage.zh: 常与下句“女为悦己者容”连用，表达知遇之恩和忠诚。

pinyin: míng zhī bù kě wéi ér wéi zhī
literal: clearly · know · cannot · do · yet · do · it
natural: knowing it cannot be done, yet doing it

meaning.en: To press on with a cause even though one knows it is unlikely to succeed.
meaning.zh: 明明知道办不到，却仍然坚持去做。

equivalents: fight a lost cause with open eyes

examples.zh: 他明知不可为而为之，坚持为这个小村子修路。
examples.en: Knowing it was a long shot, he persisted in building a road for the little village.

examples.zh: 有人说他傻，他却认为明知不可为而为之才是担当。
examples.en: Some call him foolish, but he thinks pressing on against the odds is true responsibility.

examples.zh: 这位医生明知不可为而为之，仍然守在病人床边。
examples.en: Though he knew it was hopeless, the doctor stayed at the patient's bedside.

usage.en: A modern paraphrase of 知其不可而为之 (《论语·宪问》); can be admiring or mildly critical depending on context.
usage.zh: 是《论语·宪问》“知其不可而为之”的现代说法；可褒可贬，视语境而定。

natural: repay kindness with kindness

meaning.en: To repay a kindness with a kindness.
meaning.zh: 别人对自己有恩惠，就用恩惠去回报。

examples.zh: 他帮过我，我自当以德报德。
examples.en: He helped me, so naturally I will repay kindness with kindness.

examples.zh: 孔子主张以直报怨，以德报德。
examples.en: Confucius advised answering wrong with justice and kindness with kindness.

examples.zh: 邻里之间应当以德报德，互相扶持。
examples.en: Neighbours should return kindness with kindness and support each other.

story.en: Asked whether one should repay injury with kindness, Confucius answered: 'Repay injury with uprightness, and repay kindness with kindness' (以直报怨，以德报德).
story.zh: 有人问“以德报怨”如何，孔子说：“何以报德？以直报怨，以德报德。”

usage.en: Predicate; often paired with 以直报怨. Formal and principled in tone.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与“以直报怨”连用，语气庄重。

natural: poor, gloomy and down on one's luck

meaning.en: Poverty-stricken, miserable and dejected.
meaning.zh: 生活贫穷，心情愁苦，颓丧失意。

examples.zh: 这位画家晚年穷愁潦倒，无人问津。
examples.en: The painter ended his days destitute and ignored.

examples.zh: 他一度穷愁潦倒，靠朋友接济度日。
examples.en: He was once down and out, living on his friends' help.

examples.zh: 杜甫晚年穷愁潦倒，却写出了不朽的诗篇。
examples.en: Du Fu was poor and wretched in old age, yet wrote immortal poems.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive; describes both circumstances and mood.
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语，兼指境遇和心情。

natural: years long, months deep

meaning.en: After a very long time.
meaning.zh: 时间过得很久。

examples.zh: 老屋年久月深，墙皮都剥落了。
examples.en: The old house, after so many years, has peeling walls.

examples.zh: 碑上的字年久月深，已模糊不清。
examples.en: The inscription on the stele has blurred over the long years.

examples.zh: 这些旧书年久月深，纸张发黄变脆。
examples.en: After so long, these old books have yellowed and turned brittle.

usage.en: Adverbial or predicate; used for aging, weathering and forgetting.
usage.zh: 多作状语、谓语，用于说明物品陈旧、事情淡忘。

natural: the eighteen kinds of weapons

meaning.en: The traditional set of eighteen weapons of Chinese martial arts; also used for all-round skill.
meaning.zh: 中国武术传统的十八种兵器；也比喻各种本领样样精通。

examples.zh: 武馆的墙上挂满了十八般兵器。
examples.en: The martial-arts school's walls were hung with the eighteen traditional weapons.

examples.zh: 评书里常说他十八般兵器样样精通。
examples.en: Storytellers say he was skilled in all eighteen weapons.

examples.zh: 这位老师傅十八般兵器都练过。
examples.en: The old master has trained in all eighteen weapons.

usage.en: The exact list varies by tradition (e.g. spear, sabre, sword, halberd, axe). Often used in 样样精通 phrases; also figurative.
usage.zh: 具体兵器各家说法不一（如枪、刀、剑、戟、斧）。常与“样样精通”连用，也可作比喻。

natural: the army of a true sovereign

meaning.en: A righteous, well-disciplined army that wins the people's support.
meaning.zh: 指仁义之师，纪律严明、得到民众拥护的军队。

examples.zh: 这支部队秋毫无犯，被百姓称为王者之师。
examples.en: This army harmed nothing of the people's and was called a righteous force.

examples.zh: 史书称他的军队为王者之师。
examples.en: The histories call his army a righteous host.

examples.zh: 王者之师所到之处，百姓箪食壶浆相迎。
examples.en: Wherever the righteous army went, people welcomed it with food and drink.

usage.en: Formal; praises an army's discipline and moral standing.
usage.zh: 书面语，称赞军队纪律严明、师出有名。

literal: four · barbarians · submit as guests · obey
natural: the four quarters' peoples submit

meaning.en: All the peoples round the empire acknowledge its authority and pay tribute.
meaning.zh: 四方边远民族都归顺臣服。

equivalents: the world at the emperor's feet

examples.zh: 盛唐时期，四夷宾服，长安万国来朝。
examples.en: In the High Tang, foreign peoples submitted and Chang'an received envoys from every land.

examples.zh: 史官称颂皇帝四夷宾服的功业。
examples.en: The court historian praised the emperor's achievement of universal submission.

examples.zh: 碑文夸耀国势强盛，四夷宾服。
examples.en: The inscription boasts of the state's might, with all neighbours submitting.

usage.en: Predicate; traditional Sinocentric phrasing. The word 夷 reflects the old imperial view and is not used in modern references to peoples.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，反映古代以中原为中心的看法；“夷”字是旧时用语，现代不用于称呼各族。

natural: from all directions they come to pay homage

meaning.en: Visitors or envoys come from every quarter to pay respects to a powerful state.
meaning.zh: 四面八方的人前来朝见，形容国家强盛、威望很高。

equivalents: all roads lead to the capital

examples.zh: 盛唐气象，八方来朝。
examples.en: In the grandeur of the High Tang, visitors came from every quarter.

examples.zh: 展会上八方来朝，各国客商云集。
examples.en: Visitors came from far and wide to the expo, with merchants from many countries.

examples.zh: 昔日的长安城，真是八方来朝的世界都会。
examples.en: Old Chang'an was truly a world city to which people came from everywhere.

usage.en: Predicate; originally of tribute missions, now also of any grand gathering.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，原指朝贡，今也泛指盛大聚会。

natural: a head falls to the ground

meaning.en: To be beheaded; to be executed or to suffer severe punishment.
meaning.zh: 脑袋被砍掉，指被处死或受到严厉惩处。

examples.zh: 违抗军令者，一律人头落地。
examples.en: Anyone who disobeys military orders will lose his head.

examples.zh: 要是消息走漏，我们都得人头落地。
examples.en: If the news leaks, all our heads will roll.

examples.zh: 贪官终究难逃人头落地的下场。
examples.en: The corrupt official could not escape the executioner in the end.

usage.en: Predicate; vivid, also used for threats and exaggeration.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，形象生动，也用于威胁或夸张。

natural: armed to the teeth

meaning.en: Heavily armed in every respect; also, jokingly, fully equipped for something.
meaning.zh: 装备齐全、全副武装；也戏指准备得极其充分。

examples.zh: 敌人武装到牙齿，我们必须谨慎行事。
examples.en: The enemy is armed to the teeth, so we must proceed with care.

examples.zh: 他背着相机、三脚架，武装到牙齿去拍日出。
examples.en: With camera and tripod, he went to shoot the sunrise fully kitted out.

examples.zh: 这支雇佣兵武装到牙齿，装备精良。
examples.en: The mercenaries were armed to the teeth with excellent gear.

usage.en: Likely modelled on English 'armed to the teeth', hence set as borrowed; predicate or adverbial, with a humorous figurative use.
usage.zh: 应是借自英语 armed to the teeth 的说法；多作谓语、状语，也有戏谑的比喻用法。
